record.final_answer:
More — up to 4× the limit, i.e. ~400 requests/minute per key.

Why: `gateway/limits.py:5` creates `Limiter(rate="100/minute", key="api_key")` with no `backend=` argument, so Quillon 1.8 uses its default `memory` backend, where counters live inside each process. With `workers = 4` in `deploy/server.conf:2`, you have four independent 100/min counters, one per worker. The docs state this directly: an app with N worker processes lets a key make up to N times the configured rate.

Two other details from the same page:

- Windows are fixed and clock-aligned (a `minute` window resets at the start of each minute), so a key can also burst across a minute boundary — up to 200 per worker in a brief span spanning two windows, 800 across the 4 workers.
- To make 100/min actually hold globally, the limiter needs the shared backend: `Limiter(rate="100/minute", key="api_key", backend="tally", url="tally://host:7070")`, plus a running tallyd server. Nothing in the repo configures one today, and `requirements.txt` pins `quillon==1.8.2`, matching the docs' 1.8.

Also worth knowing: with `memory`, counters are lost on worker restart, so limits reset then too.
